summary: An excerpt from Kate Douglas Wiggin's novel Rebecca of Sunnybrook Farm (Book 11, part 45), in which Rebecca and uncle Jerry Cobb discuss her aunts Mirandy and Jane after a rain shower. Rebecca decides to give up the planned river drive and return to aunt Mirandy's house, and Jerry insists on going with her to settle things. The passage is written in dialect and carries the warm, humorous tone typical of the book.
one_line: Rebecca, feeling pressed by her aunt Mirandy, resolves to return home after a rainbow-lit conversation with uncle Jerry Cobb.
key_facts: Rebecca says she gets along splendidly with aunt Jane, who is 'just as good and kind as she can be'.
Rebecca says aunt Jane 'can't stand up for me against aunt Mirandy; she's about as afraid of her as I am.'
Jane reportedly told Sarah that she is keeping a sewing school and that her scholar has made three dresses.
Jane said she has taken a class in Sunday-school and means to go to the picnic with Rebecca.
A silence in the little kitchen is broken only by the ticking of the tall clock and the beating of Rebecca's heart.
A rainbow arch appears through the window after the rain ceases, spanning the heavens 'like a radiant bridge'.
Rebecca thinks bridges take one across difficult places, and that uncle Jerry seems to have built one over her troubles.
Uncle Jerry says the shower 'washed the face o' the airth nice an' clean' and that everything will shine tomorrow when he and Rebecca are driving up river.
Rebecca pushes her cup away, rises, and puts on her hat and jacket quietly.
Rebecca tells Mr. Cobb, 'I'm not going to drive up river,' and says she is going back now while she has the courage.
Rebecca says she does not know whether aunt Mirandy will take her in after she has run away.
Rebecca asks Mr. Cobb if he would go with her back to aunt Mirandy's.
Uncle Jerry replies that he does not propose to leave until he gets 'this thing fixed up'.
Uncle Jerry says Mirandy will be real sorry to find Rebecca gone, and that Jane would set great store by Rebecca's company.
